_meta.purpose: WARP_MANIFEST_V1 §10 conformance — measure where the server's stdlib html.parser asset enumerator (warp._enumerate_manifest_assets) diverges from what a spec-compliant HTML parser (a browser) would load on initial page load.
_meta.derived_from: html5lib-tests (https://github.com/html5lib/html5lib-tests, tree-construction/) and the WHATWG HTML parsing spec content models. Cases are hand-distilled to the asset-enumeration question and reduced to minimal markup; they are NOT verbatim upstream fixtures.
_meta.coverage_note: expected_assets is the browser-loaded set (spec ground truth). xfail=true marks a KNOWN divergence of the stdlib html.parser from that ground truth — the honest coverage gap, not a bug to hide. xfail=false cases MUST match or the enumerator regressed.
_meta.class_note: class is one of HTML/JS/CSS/CSS_IMPORT; the HTML document itself is not listed (it is always covered).

cases.name: script_inside_template_is_inert
cases.divergence: html.parser has no <template> content model — it surfaces the inner <script src> as a normal start tag, so warp OVER-enumerates an asset a browser never loads.

cases.name: stylesheet_inside_head_noscript_is_raw_text
cases.divergence: With scripting enabled a browser treats <noscript> content in <head> as raw text, so the <link> is not an element and n.css is not loaded. html.parser parses it as an element, so warp OVER-enumerates.

cases.name: character_reference_in_src
cases.note: CONFORMANT: html.parser unescapes character references in attribute values regardless of convert_charrefs (which only governs text nodes), so & → & and the resolved URL matches the browser.

cases.name: duplicate_src_keeps_first_per_spec
cases.divergence: The HTML spec drops a duplicate attribute (first wins). warp collapses attrs into a dict, so the LAST src wins — the enumerated URL can differ.
